sentences.text: Bohaiornis is a genus of extinct birds belonging to the subclass Enantiornithes.

The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — preserved two long, ribbon-like tail feathers rather than a fan of shorter ones, and the animal was significantly larger than its relative Eoenantiornis.
The original description relied on a well-preserved, fully articulated skeleton of a subadult individual.
A second, larger specimen contained several rock-like structures inside its abdominal cavity that researchers initially thought were gastroliths.
However, later analysis proved these were mineral concretions formed after death, not stones swallowed for digestion.
Dongyu Hu, Li Li, Lianhaim Hou, and Xing Xu named the genus and its only known species, Bohaiornis guoi, in 2011.
A second, larger specimen was described in 2014.
Bohaiornis is the type genus of the family Bohaiornithidae, and Bohaiornis guoi serves as the type species for the genus.
The Paleobiology Database classifies Bohaiornis under the class Reptilia.
Fossils of this bird have been found in the Lower Cretaceous Jiufotang Formation and Yixian Formation in western Liaoning, China, dating to the Aptian stage between 121.4 and 113.2 million years ago.
